I live in Bogun county, Iowa. Ugly, run down sort of place. It's an odd duck of an area, where the corn doesn't grow, and the soybeans are nowhere to be seen.

Corvill is the name of the once great metropolis I live in. My father used to tell me of how industry had once inhabited Corvill, how Phantoma/Neuromatics had provided jobs, and security to the people of my hometown.

All that's left of Phantoma these days is the lone building jutting into the sky. A reminder of a once great empire, reduced to bankruptcy. They saw fear in a handful of dust, it seemed, and left real quick after that..

So, with all the decline, all the stagnation, I began to wonder what was wrong with Corvill. So I started driving. And driving. And driving.

There was no way out. I kept driving, till my tank was nearly empty, but there was no way out.

The road led to a sign that said "You are now entering Corvill", but I had been driving for an hour away from Corvill. I broke down that day, started sobbing, thinking I was never going to leave this piece of shit town. There's nothing here for me.

So I began to wonder what it was that goddamned town wanted me for. I spoke to my mother and father, they stonewalled me. I had spoken to my friends, but everyone in this goddamned town was so slack-jawed and vacant. Old Man Winters told me in a drunken haze that they're putting something in the water, told me to go to Phantoma/Neuromatics.

And so I broke into Phantoma/Neuromatics.. I had heard rumors about it, been told by my mother and father a thousand times never to go in it, but it was the only thing I could think of.

Dusty, rotten smelling building, copper stripped out of the walls. But I couldn't help but think that this place had been nice when it was up and running. This wasn't a regular sort of building. There had been some serious equipment. Now, it was all trashed and fouled beyond recognition, but this stuff had been worth a pretty penny.

I followed the smell of decay to a cage full of dead... something, whatever it was. I didn't want to know. I wasn't stupid enough to get close to it.

I found a note on a desk, and began to read. After that, I really began to wonder what the fuck was going on. It read:

""I remember when the fledgling company was started with a hope, and a dream. A dream of making the world better, to improve the human race. It was January 2nd, 1979.

I can recall the owner, a man named Rigdon, with his bushy beard and crazed eyes, telling us "This is it, this is the next step in the evolutionary process for mankind.". What fools we were to believe him. We were idealistic young men in those days, not a touch of grey in our hair, nor any doubt of our ability. Full of vigor and hubris, we proceeded in our studies.

We should have known better. The experiments were never meant to come to term, not at those stages. The surrogate mothers were just a test of the RN compound... That goddamned compound which has caused us all so many horrors and nightmares. The subjects were too human. Too human, and too powerful. We found out what they could do when we caught a lab tech staring one day, transfixed, cutting his own throat with a straight razor. It was then that we realized the true danger of these animals, and of the compound.

That was why we are shutting down. Hopefully, these animals have died off. The mutation rate of the animals was too high, and they must have died by now. I can only hope and pray. By the end of it, they looked nothing of the apes we had brought in. They were changing. Changing into something sentient, and malevolent.

I can only shudder at thinking of what would happen if Ms. Mayfield ever had kids. She managed to inject herself with the compound while experimenting. As far as we know, it shouldn't effect her, the actions of the compound being expressed only in the next generation, but her child.. She must never have children."

My mother's maiden name was Mayfield.. It couldn't be.

Old Man Winters knows about it too. I'm not crazy, though I thought I was for a while.

I spoke to the old bastard, gave him a bottle of whiskey to loosen his tongue.

"Town what'rent always like this. Was a mining town back'n the older days, 'fore them eggheads stuck us here so we couldn't get out."

"What do you mean?"

"There is no Bogun county. See, I told'yer to go up'ter them that Phantoma buildin', you see what you needed to see?"

"I don't understand. What does Phantoma have to do with Bogun county?"

"They invented it! They're what're keepin' us in here! No one can leave, goddamn it! I've tried myself, a hundred damned times. It's cause they're keeping things in here what'n they don't want out. You're the Mayfield kid, ain't ya? You'll figure it sooner or later, I guess. Once the change comes over you atleast." The change? Like what the note in the Phantoma/Neuromatics building had spoken about?

"What change?"

"You'll find out soon enough, I suppose. Ain't like you're any different from the monkeys. I used to work at Phantoma, myself. I knew your mother, a'yup. You were never supposed to happen, you know."

"What the fuck is that supposed to mean?! You've got about three seconds to tell me what you're on about, before I knock your teeth down your throat."

"You're an aggressive sort, aren't you? The test subjects always were."

"Why are you telling me this?"

"Cancer, kiddo. A life working for those callous bastards isn't good for the health. They weren't exactly OSHA compliant. I'm a dead man anyways. They kill me, they're just killing an old man."

"So what are you telling me?"

"Phantoma/Neuromatics made you, kid. They made you, and they keep you here so you don't get out. There's something inside you that most folks don't have."

"My father-"

"...Is very heavily drugged. Just like everyone else in this town. Why do you think the tap water is so bitter? Why do you have memory problems? Can you remember what you did on your last birthday?"

"This is crazy. This is absolute lunacy."

"It's not normal, that's for sure. So I bet you're wondering how to get out."

"How?"

"You have to figure out what they don't want you to know."

"I'm just a normal guy. I don't have any hidden ability, or special powers. I can't use the force, this isn't a goddamned movie!"

"There are things inside the human potential that would surprise you. If you don't believe me, go back to the old Phantoma building. You'll find proof there."

Soon, I would learn more than I ever wanted to know.
